Subject: Hybrid hosting attestation + VPC controls for SOC2/SIG - PineBridge

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team has a short list of evidentiary items to close the SIG/SOC2 questionnaire for our pilot. Were specifically gating on:

- Confirmation that production customer data for our tenant will remain in AWS us-east-1 by default, with optional EU processing only when explicitly enabled and governed by a contractual addendum.
- Details on private connectivity: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink options, expected IP ranges, and whether cross-account peering is used for any control plane traffic.
- Proof that there is no automatic cross-region replication of customer data and where KV cache snapshots (if any) are stored.
- KMS key management model: do you support customer-managed keys where the CMK never leaves customer account? Any split-key (dual-control) options?

Can you provide a short attestation doc and a runbook/stub that describes how VPC peering/PrivateLink is configured and how failover is handled? Ideally something we can attach to the SIG evidence bundle.

Thanks — if you can get this over by next Wednesday (8/25) thatd be ideal.

— Rachel

Head of Security Programs, PineBridge Health
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Rachel Summers <rachel@pinebridgehealth.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hybrid hosting attestation + VPC controls for SOC2/SIG - PineBridge

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear list. Looping in Neha (security/compliance) and Priyom (solutions) to assemble the artifacts. High level answers below; well attach the formal attestation + runbook as requested.

1) Data residency default and opt-in EU processing
- Default: tenant data for new accounts in PineBridge will be served from AWS us-east-1.
- EU processing: available only via explicit customer request + contractual amendment (we do not auto-enable EU copies). We will include the contract language in the attestation PDF.

2) Private connectivity model
- We support both VPC peering (customer-owned VPC <-> Redwood-managed service VPC) and AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints).
- For PrivateLink we provision an interface endpoint in the customer's VPC; control plane metadata remains in Redwood control plane but data plane traffic flows over the endpoint.
- No cross-account public IP exposure — we use private IP ranges and recommend using customer security groups to restrict source ranges.

3) Cross-region replication and KV cache
- We do not perform automatic cross-region replication of customer data. KV caches are ephemeral in-memory caches on serving nodes; snapshots are not persisted across regions unless explicitly enabled for a customer and documented in the contract.

4) KMS model
- We offer customer-managed KMS integration: customer provides a CMK in their AWS account and grants Redwood a restricted-encrypt/decrypt role for keys used at rest. The CMK remains in the customer account.
- For higher assurance customers we support a split-key pattern (customer CMK + Redwood escrow key) — described in the attestation doc.

Action items: Neha and Priyom will produce a one-page attestation PDF, a VPC operational runbook (peering example + PrivateLink steps), and an architecture diagram showing KMS flow.

Ill follow up shortly with the attachments.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Quick clarifications:

- Control plane traffic (scheduling/monitoring) traverses our control plane; sensitive customer payloads never traverse the control plane in plaintext.
- For transit-failure scenarios we include an automated fallback policy that will route to a cold-standby in the same region (no automatic cross-region failover unless expressly configured in the SLA). Runbook includes exact failover steps and required IAM permissions.

Links included in the PDF point to our internal runbook (read-only Drive link) and to the SOC2 control mapping table. If you want we can produce a redacted SOC2 excerpt for the SIG bundle.
